name: Soundscape Theory
citation: Schafer, R.M. (1977). The soundscape: Our sonic environment and the tuning of the world. Destiny Books.

constructs.description: Same dBA produces different evaluations by context. Context-modulated perception via PP prediction error.
The right sounds reduce annoyance despite higher total SPL. Biophilic sounds (birdsong, water) produce dopaminergic reward via NM.
Match between expected and actual soundscape predicts restoration. Park context generates expectation for birdsong-like spectra; match = low acoustic PE.
Sustained >55 dBA produces cortisol and cardiovascular effects via HPA activation. Body-budget threat via IC.

irreducible_residual.narrative: Irreducible residual ~25%: cultural specification of soundscape categories (~15% — what counts as 'pleasant' varies substantially by culture) and spectrotemporal complexity preferences (~10%). The IE-DPT contribution is critical: a construction worker habituated to 85 dBA finds 60 dBA unremarkable; a librarian finds it distressing — the explicit channel sets the activity frame and expectation model.
